method split_words(txt: string) returns (result: seq<string>)
    requires txt != null
    ensures (forall i: int :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> (result[i] != "")) // Each word in the result is non-empty
    ensures (|result| > 0 ==> (exists x: string :: x in result && x != "")) // There is at least one non-empty word if result is not empty
    ensures (|result| == 0 ==> (txt == "")) // If result is empty, input must be empty
    ensures (|result| > 0 ==> (forall x: string :: x in result ==> (x.split(" ") != null || x.split(",") != null))) // Result is derived from splitting on whitespace or commas
    ensures (|result| == 0 ==> count_lowercase_odd(txt) >= 0) // If no words are returned, the count of lowercase letters with odd order is non-negative
    ensures (|result| == 0 ==> count_lowercase_odd(txt) == count_lowercase_letters(txt)) // If no words, return the count of lowercase letters with odd order
    ensures (|result| == 0 ==> count_lowercase_letters(txt) == count_lowercase_letters_odd(txt)) // No words means counting lowercase letters corresponds to counting odd alphabetical ones

method count_lowercase_odd(txt: string) returns (count: int)
    requires txt != null
    ensures count >= 0
    ensures count == Count(i | 0 <= i < |txt| && is_lowercase_odd(txt[i])) // Count is the number of lowercase letters with odd order

method is_lowercase_odd(c: char) returns (result: bool)
    requires c >= 'a' && c <= 'z'
    ensures result == (ord(c) % 2 == 1) // Character is lowercase and has an odd order in alphabet
```
